essays.title: Psychosis: first episode and predisposing factors

sections.title: What psychosis is, and how a delusion is defined
sections.intent: Fix the terms before using them. Definition first, with its source named.

sections.title: Psychosis on a transdiagnostic continuum
sections.intent: The model that lets risk be discussed below the diagnostic threshold.

sections.title: The prodrome and the first episode
sections.intent: The window in which onset happens, and what subthreshold symptoms predict.

sections.title: Predisposing factors
sections.intent: What raises risk: neurodevelopmental, behavioural, environmental. The essay's title promises this section, so it carries the most weight.

sections.title: Assessing risk, and what the instruments cannot say
sections.intent: PQ-B and its kind. A screening threshold is not a clinical determination.

sections.title: Treatment, and why CBTp underperforms for delusions
sections.intent: Guideline-recommended, small-to-moderate effect. Say why.

sections.title: Coping as the active ingredient
sections.intent: The mechanism the treatment section implies: coping mediates exacerbation.

essays.title: Vignette: internet and AI use as a predicating factor

sections.title: The vignette
sections.intent: The case the essay argues from. Published cases sit here as models and as corroboration, not as the vignette itself.

sections.title: The scale of exposure
sections.intent: Establish a population-level exposure, with real adoption data.

sections.title: This is not new: pathoplastic, not pathogenic
sections.intent: The intellectual core. Influencing machines since 1810; technology has shaped delusional content for two centuries. Concede this before claiming anything.

sections.title: Naming it: AI-related psychosis, and its contested status
sections.intent: Define the term, say whose definition it is, and that it is descriptive rather than diagnostic.

sections.title: Why this technology invites it
sections.intent: What is actually different this time: a fluent, agreeable, second-person interlocutor. Mindless social response, sycophancy, misread referentiality, and the documented failures that stop this being theoretical.

sections.title: What the evidence actually shows
sections.intent: The empirical core, with the cross-sectional limit stated in the authors' own words. Survey base rates, then the clinical tail.

sections.title: First episode and the developmental window
sections.intent: Where the two essays meet: peak adoption age meets peak onset age, and the clinical data points the same way.

sections.title: The other side
sections.intent: Access, waitlists, companionship, changing attitudes. Held after the risk so the essay is not a one-sided alarm.

sections.title: Assessment and practice implications
sections.intent: Digital-use history, technological literacy, screening, early intervention.
